raw.raw:
The spectral hand drifts forward. Touches his shoulder.

He moves.

Not dead then.

He pulls away from the touch with a sound. Low. Ragged. Not quite a word. His eyes open and they're wrong, the pupils blown wide and dark in the green light, too much white showing at the edges.

Two years against that stone. Looking at whatever the terminus shows you when you look too long.

The hand touches him again. Gentle.

He focuses. Slow. Like watching ice melt.

His mouth moves.

"Is it," he starts. Stops. Tries again. "Is it going to flood."

Not a question exactly. More like something he's been sitting with for a while.

You crouch at the bottom of the stairs. Keep distance. Give him room.

His face is gaunt but not starved. The cave has tidal pools. Something to drink. Something to eat if you weren't particular. He's been surviving. Barely. On purpose or by accident, hard to say.

He looks at the terminus stone behind him. Then back at you.

"I couldn't leave," he says. "Once I understood what it was." A pause. "Someone had to stay. In case."

In case someone came down the stairs.

[QUEST_STEP:Assault on Thistletop|Neutralise the threat below the waterline|true]

Old habit. Good one.

[DICE:Perception check|17|success]

You read the cave in sections. Left to right. Methodical.

The tidal pools are still. Green light comes from bioluminescence in the water itself, something living in it, small and harmless. The walls are wet but not actively weeping. Tide is out. An hour, maybe two, before that changes.

One entrance. The stairs behind you. One exit. A fissure in the far wall, low, maybe three feet high, sea smell pouring through it. Too small for a person. Barely.

The terminus stone itself is carved on all four faces. Same spiral. Same script. The fluid from the channels above doesn't reach here yet. Just the stone and the intent of it.

No threats.

Nothing waiting in the shadows. Nothing in the pools. Whatever breathed in here eight months ago when Shalelu pressed her ear to the rock, it's gone now. Or it's quiet. Or it never left but it doesn't care about you.

Aldus Vareth watches you scan the room. He recognises what you're doing.

"Nothing comes in from the sea," he says. "Not anymore." A long pause. "Something used to."

He doesn't elaborate. His hands are braced against the terminus stone like he needs it to sit upright.

"Who sent you," he says.

"Who sent you here originally?"

He looks at you for a long moment. Weighing something.

"Hemwick," he says.

There it is.

"Two years ago. Maybe more. Time moves strange down here." His hands shift against the stone. "He said someone needed to watch the terminus. That the mechanism above was destabilising. That if the reservoir discharged without a witness at the stone, the dissolution would be." He stops. "Incomplete."

"Incomplete how."

"The contract requires a witness." He says it like he's recited it before. To himself, in the dark, counting the tides. "The Mouth of Account doesn't close without one. Whatever discharges has to be received. Acknowledged. Otherwise it just." Another stop. "Disperses. Into the water table. Into the rock. Ten thousand years of accumulated greed bleeding into the sea." His eyes are clearer now. The blown pupils settling. "Hemwick said that would be very bad."

You think about Hemwick upstairs. Calm. Informative. Cooperative in that particular way that makes you feel managed.

Aldus reads your face.

"He's not wrong," he says. "About the mechanism. Whatever else he is." A beat. "I did wonder, eventually, whether someone was ever actually coming."

He looks at the fissure in the far wall.

"The tide," he says. "How long do we have."

Something moves in his face. Not relief. Harder than that.

"Yourself," he repeats.

"Myself."

He looks down at his hands. Still braced against the stone. Two years of that posture. It's probably automatic now.

"Hemwick said someone would come," he says quietly. "Sent by the Collector. Part of the arrangement." A pause. "He didn't say someone would come on their own."

He looks up.

"That's different."

You don't tell him how different. You don't tell him about Daeris upstairs, or the service contract, or the creature in the doorway that stepped aside without being asked. You let him sit with it.

"The terms," he says eventually. "Do you know them?"

"Four channels. Junction stone. Witness at the terminus."

His breath comes out slow. A long exhale. Something he's been holding.

"Then you actually came to finish it." Not a question. "Not to observe. Not to manage." He straightens slightly against the stone. First time in a while, probably. "To finish it."

He looks around the cave. The green light on the pools. The wet walls. The fissure breathing sea air.

"I've been down here a long time," he says. "I'd like to leave."

The tide will turn in under an hour.

"Soon," you say. "Stay at the stone."

He nods. Like he expected nothing else.

You turn back to the stairs. Message upward, Frizwick first.

"We found him. Alive. He's at the terminus. Tell Morwen. Start the sequence."

A breath. Then Frizwick's voice, quiet and close as a secret. "Understood. Daeris is awake. Calm. Morwen's already at the first channel."

Good.

You look back at Aldus.

"When it starts," you say, "what do you feel?"

He considers that seriously.

"The stone gets warm," he says. "Then the light changes. Then it's loud, but not with sound." He presses his palm flat against the spiral carving. "Then it's over."

"You've seen it before."

"I've seen it almost happen. Three times." A pause. "Nualia twice. Someone else before her. They never had a witness here." His jaw tightens. "They never finished the sequence."

Upstairs, somewhere above you, Morwen is reading channel script by blue-white light. Frizwick has the charges. The creature is watching the doorway.

Everything is in place.

Almost.

[QUEST_STEP:Assault on Thistletop|Witness the dissolution at the terminus stone|false]
[QUEST:Assault on Thistletop|completed]
[XP:800]

"The others who came before. What happened to them."

Aldus doesn't answer immediately. His thumb traces the spiral carving. Old habit.

"The first one I saw was a woman," he says. "Robed. She got as far as the junction chamber. The creature stopped her. Not violently. Just." He pauses. "Stood in the way. She didn't understand the contract terms. Tried to force it. Left."

"And the second."

"A man. Collector's agent, I think. He understood the terms well enough. Got through the creature. Got down here." Aldus looks at the fissure. "Stood where you're standing. Read the stone. Then decided the dissolution was worth more incomplete than finished." A flat pause. "He had a buyer for the reservoir contents. Ten thousand years of concentrated greed. Someone was paying."

"What happened to him."

"The tide came in early." Aldus says it without inflection. "Or it seemed early. Hard to know, down here."

The fissure breathes cold salt air.

You don't ask him to clarify.

Above you, the hum from the mechanism shifts pitch. Barely. Just enough.

Morwen has started on the channels.

The stone under Aldus's palm brightens. Faint. Green going gold at the edges.

It's beginning.

[ARC_COMPLETE:Thistletop]
[XP:500]
[STORY_BEAT:The dissolution sequence begins; Thistletop's Thassilonian reservoir moves toward release after ten thousand years of accumulation]

You cross the cave. Sit beside him against the stone.

It's warm. Already. Through your leather.

Aldus doesn't comment on the company. Just shifts slightly to make room. Two years alone and he's forgotten the etiquette of it, or past caring.

The green light deepens. Gold threading through it now. Coming from the stone itself, from the script, each carved line filling like a vessel.

The hum is different down here. Not mechanical. Not sound exactly. It lives in the back teeth. In the sternum.

"First channel," Aldus says quietly.

You feel it before you understand it. A pulse through the stone. Clean. Decisive.

Then silence where there wasn't silence before. One voice in a choir dropping out.

Somewhere above, Morwen cut the first feed line.

Aldus exhales.

"Three more," he says.

You wait. The tide pool nearest the fissure stirs. Not wind. Something below registering the change. The water settles.

The stone brightens another degree.

Then the second pulse hits.

Harder. The whole cave shudders once, like a dog shaking off water. Dust from the ceiling. The pools ripple outward in perfect circles.

Aldus grips the stone with both hands.

"That's two," he says. Steadier than he looks. "She's fast."

[FUTURE_EVENT_RESOLVED:Four intake channels must be severed in sequence before the junction stone can be struck to initiate dissolution]

Three comes quieter than two.

A clean severance. No shudder. Just a drop in pressure, like a room losing a fire. The gold in the script brightens to compensate. Hungry. Ready.

Aldus has both hands flat on the stone now. Eyes closed.

"One left," he says.

You put your back against the terminus stone. Feel the whole weight of what's above you. Ten thousand years of it. Greed and hunger and desperate wanting, compressed into rock and channel and this one carved spiral. Thassilon at its worst, distilled and stored.

And Morwen upstairs, cutting it loose with cold hands and a fieldwork journal.

The fourth pulse is nothing like the others.

It doesn't shake the cave. It doesn't make sound. It just arrives. Everywhere at once. In the stone, in the air, in the space behind your eyes. A pressure that builds for three full seconds and then.

Releases.

The terminus stone goes white.

Aldus makes a sound. Not pain. Not fear. Something older than both.

The discharge comes downward through the rock. You feel it pass through you like a wind that doesn't move air. Like something vast recognising you and moving on. It hits the stone. The spiral swallows it. The Mouth of Account opens and receives ten thousand years of accumulated human wanting.

Then it closes.

Silence.

Real silence.

Aldus slumps sideways against you. Breathing.

"Done," he says.

[QUEST:The Dissolution of Thistletop|completed]
[XP:600]
[STORY_BEAT:The Thassilonian reservoir empties; ten thousand years of harvested greed discharges into the terminus stone and is consumed]
[FUTURE_EVENT_RESOLVED:Descend one to two levels and sever the active intake channels to starve the reservoir mechanism before threshold is reached]

Nothing comes.

The stone is cold again. Already. Like it was never anything else.

The script is dark. Every carved line empty. Ten thousand years of purpose, spent in four heartbeats. Whatever architecture Thassilon built this place to serve, it's finished with that now.

Aldus breathes. Slowly. Like a man remembering how.

The tide pools are still. The fissure breathes salt air. That's all.

You hold the blade anyway. Old habit. Good habit.

A minute passes. Two.

Then footsteps on the stair. Measured. Familiar.

Morwen comes through the low arch first. Chalk dust on her hands. A cut on her forearm she hasn't addressed. Her eyes sweep the chamber, land on you, land on the dark terminus stone.

She reads it the way she reads everything. Quickly. Completely.

"Clean," she says.

Not a question.

Frizwick comes through behind her. She looks at the stone, at Aldus, at your blade. Sheathes her own. Decision made.

Morwen crouches in front of Aldus. Studies his face with the dispassion of someone cataloguing damage.

"Can you walk," she says.

Aldus considers this seriously. "Yes."

"Then we're leaving." She stands. Looks at you. "Hemwick is still tied to a bracket upstairs."

Right. Him.

You press your free hand flat against it.

Cold. Smooth. The carved spiral is still there, still deep, still precise. Ten thousand years of craft doesn't vanish with the contents.

But the script is empty. Every line that was filling with gold, dark now. Not damaged. Not erased. Just done. Like a vessel after pouring.

You trace the outermost ring with two fingers. The stone doesn't respond. No warmth. No hum. No sense of anything remaining inside that wants something from you.

One mark catches your eye.

Near the base. Below the spiral. Almost at floor level, where the stone meets the cave rock. Not Thassilonian. Newer. Cut with a knife, not a mason's tool.

A name. Rough letters. ALDUS. And below it, three tallies. Then a gap. Then a fourth.

He'd been keeping count of the failed attempts. Including, apparently, his own expected failure.

You glance at him. He's watching you.

"I was bored," he says flatly.

Morwen makes a sound that isn't quite a laugh.

The chamber has nothing else to offer. The mechanism is spent. The creature upstairs has no more work to tend. Whatever Thistletop was built to be, it's been something else for ten thousand years.

Now it's just stone and salt water.

Time to go up.

GM: You cross the cave. Sit beside him against the stone.

It's warm. Already. Through your leather.

Aldus doesn't comment on the company. Just shifts slightly to make room. Two years alone and he's forgotten the etiquette of it, or past caring.

The green light deepens. Gold threading through it now. Coming from the stone itself, from the script, each carved line filling like a vessel.

The hum is different down here. Not mechanical. Not sound exactly. It lives in the back teeth. In the sternum.

"First channel," Aldus says quietly.

You feel it before you understand it. A pulse through the stone. Clean. Decisive.

Then silence where there wasn't silence before. One voice in a choir dropping out.

Somewhere above, Morwen cut the first feed line.

Aldus exhales.

"Three more," he says.

You wait. The tide pool nearest the fissure stirs. Not wind. Something below registering the change. The water settles.

The stone brightens another degree.

Then the second pulse hits.

Harder. The whole cave shudders once, like a dog shaking off water. Dust from the ceiling. The pools ripple outward in perfect circles.

Aldus grips the stone with both hands.

"That's two," he says. Steadier than he looks. "She's fast."

Player: Stay with Aldus; witness the dissolution from here.
GM: Three comes quieter than two.

A clean severance. No shudder. Just a drop in pressure, like a room losing a fire. The gold in the script brightens to compensate. Hungry. Ready.

Aldus has both hands flat on the stone now. Eyes closed.

"One left," he says.

You put your back against the terminus stone. Feel the whole weight of what's above you. Ten thousand years of it. Greed and hunger and desperate wanting, compressed into rock and channel and this one carved spiral. Thassilon at its worst, distilled and stored.
